subject: Dedicated capacity: Halcyon deal - GPU runway & tokens/sec simulation
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia@halcyonhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity kickoff — Halcyon / Redwood

Hi Mina,

Thanks for making time today. We want to make the Dedicated commit decision in the next 3 weeks and need a pragmatic runway estimate for GPUs so our procurement team can size the budget. High-level profile below — I've attached the usage snapshot and expected distribution in the sheet ("halcyon_request_profile.xlsx"):

- Peak DAU window: 12,000 active users/hour (30% of daily traffic)
- Expected concurrent interactive sessions during peak: ~600 (web clients invoking completion API)
- Average response length: 280 tokens (median), 95th percentile 1,100 tokens
- Typical interactive pattern: multi-turn chat, average session 3 calls, typical think-time 6–12s
- Availability target: p99 latency < 600ms for streaming-first workload; offline batch and long-form use can tolerate higher latency

Questions for Redwood: can you model tokens/sec at peak and give a recommended Dedicated commit (GPUs) with headroom for 99th pct latency and for business-critical peak bursts? Also please call out a conservative fallback plan (smaller model or routing to hosted layer) in case we overshoot.

Appreciate a short model and numbers that we can share internally.

Best,
Olivia
Director of Product — Halcyon Health

Attachments: halcyon_request_profile.xlsx (spreadsheet, 34 KB)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@halcyonhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity kickoff — Halcyon / Redwood

Hi Olivia — thanks for the profile and the sheet. I sketched a short tokens/sec runway using the numbers you provided; attaching the populated sheet and a one-page summary. Key assumptions I used (please flag if different):

- Peak concurrent calls: 600 (from your note)
- Avg tokens per call during peak: 280 tokens
- Average generation time per call: 6s (reflects streaming-first UX)
- Peak tokens/sec = concurrent * (avg_tokens / avg_generation_time) = 600 * (280 / 6) ≈ 28,000 tokens/sec

Model performance assumptions (baseline — we can refine with a short perf run):
- rw-13b-v2 (fp16) on an A100-80GB equivalent: ~1,400 tokens/sec under client-aware batching for typical chat sequences
- rw-13b-v2 (q4_k_m) quantized variant: ~850 tokens/sec but can increase peak latency variance (worse p99)
- Smaller model (rw-6b or instruction-tuned 6B) for fallback: ~2,500 tokens/sec per GPU (lower quality)

Raw GPU headcount math (no utilization or headroom applied):
- Using fp16 perf: 28,000 / 1,400 ≈ 20 GPUs
- Using q4 perf: 28,000 / 850 ≈ 33 GPUs

Operational multipliers to convert to commit recommendation:
- Sustained utilization target: 0.80 (leave room for OS/serving jitter, maintenance)
- Production headroom for burst and p99 SLO: 1.20 factor (20% headroom above modeled peak)

Applying multipliers (recommended commit = ceil(raw / utilization * headroom)):
- fp16 path: ceil(20 / 0.80 * 1.20) ≈ ceil(30) = 30 GPUs
- q4 path: ceil(33 / 0.80 * 1.20) ≈ ceil(50) = 50 GPUs

Recommendation summary:
- If Halcyon prioritizes p99 latency and quality: commit 30 GPUs (A100-equivalent) running fp16 rw-13b-v2. This gives ~20–25% runway for short spikes and keeps most p99s under 500–600ms with client-aware batching and prefix caching.
- If Halcyon prefers cost-minimized commit with quantized models: commit 50 GPUs but expect p99s to increase and more complex fallback behavior.
- Conservative commercial option: commit 35 GPUs (fp16) + 15 GPU burst pool (on-demand) to balance cost and buffer weekends/events.

Fallbacks and routing:
- Auto-fallback to rw-6b for non-critical requests (approx 3x tokens/sec improvement, lower quality).
- Route overflow to Hosted pool during >2x expected peak for short windows (we can reserve burst credits for that).

Next steps: can you confirm regional split (US/EU) and whether the 600 concurrent is global or per-region? I've attached the spreadsheet (halcyon_request_profile.xlsx) with the token simulation and a cost sketch for the three scenarios.

Mina
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: halcyon_request_profile.xlsx (updated, 78 KB); halcyon_sla_draft_v1.pdf (SLA stubs)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity kickoff — Halcyon / Redwood

Adding some infra-level notes to Mina's numbers — these will change the effective tokens/sec depending on sequence distribution and KV cache hit rates:

- Sequence length distribution matters: heavy tail (many 1,000+ token generations) will reduce effective throughput significantly because long sequences hold KV cache and occupy slots longer. If 10% of requests are >1,000 tokens, plan an additional 10–15% headroom beyond the math Mina used.
- KV cache memory: 13B fp16 model requires ~12–14 GB per concurrent KV state (depends on tokens). For 600 concurrent sessions, ensure aggregated KV memory per GPU doesn't oversubscribe - sharding to multiple GPUs per model replica may be necessary.
- Batching model: Aim for dynamic batching with an upper latency bound of 80–100ms to maintain p99 targets; this typically yields the 1,200–1,600 tokens/sec numbers Mina referenced on A100-class hardware.
- Sizing playbook: Recommend a Dedicated pool with: 30 committed GPUs (fp16), a warm-spare buffer of 10 GPUs (_warm_, not billed as commit but warmed for fast scale), and 15 GPUs as on-demand burst for marketing events. Implement automatic fallback policy to quantized variant when queue length > X.

Operational asks for Halcyon engineering: please provide realistic per-session sequence histograms (tokens per turn and turns per session) and any expected batch inference patterns (e.g., background transcription/embedding workloads). Those will let us tighten the estimate.

Marcus
Principal Systems Engineer — Redwood Inference

Thanks for the model and the ops notes. Quick exec summary for the commercial thread so they can prep an LOI:

- Recommendation for Halcyon (p99-focused): Commit 30 A100-equivalent GPUs running fp16 rw-13b-v2. Estimated steady-state tokens/sec headroom handles typical peaks; projected p99s ~450–550ms with our batching and caching.
- Commercial fallback option: 35 GPU commit + 15 GPU burst pool (preferred for conservative runway).
- Cost sketch (ballpark): committed pool ~ $68k–$92k / month depending on reserved pricing term and region (we'll produce a precise quote once region split confirmed).

Action items:
1) Mina: produce a one-page commit slide (numbers + recommended commercial bullets) for Halcyon's procurement. Include the breakouts: fp16 30 GPU plan, 35+15 fallback, and a q4 route for cost-sensitive workloads.
2) Marcus: capture the sequence histogram impact and a short playbook for KV memory checks so Halcyon's infra team can validate fit.
3) Olivia: confirm regional split (US vs EU) and call out any regulatory constraints (data residency) — that affects where Dedicated pools live and pricing.

I'll loop in SalesOps after we have the region breakdown and the finalized one-pager.

Rishi
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
